short: An English king whose contested succession sparked nearly two decades of civil war.
full:
Following the death of his uncle Henry I in December 1135, Stephen of Blois crossed the Channel and seized the English throne, preempting the designated heir, Empress Matilda. Although he secured the treasury and the support of the church, his right to rule was violently contested. His reign was defined by the Anarchy, a protracted civil war against Matilda's supporters that devastated vast areas of the country.

Stephen was an active military commander but struggled to exert definitive control over his fractured kingdom. He was captured at the Battle of Lincoln in 1141 and briefly deposed before being restored. Unable to secure the succession for his own son, he was forced by the 1153 Treaty of Wallingford to recognise Matilda's son, Henry Plantagenet, as his heir, ending his troubled reign.
